sources.appraisal: Publisher full-text Results and Table 1 examined. Same cohort as Enes 2024, not independent; strain includes exposure, correlations exploratory.

claims.assertion: In the male trial, the two scheduled escalation groups improved squat 1RM more than the fixed-set group.
claims.limitations: 37 randomized, 31 completed; small groups; all started at 22 quadriceps sets, cumulative assigned sets 264/384/444; no dose-matched trajectory comparator; additional high-intensity lower-body exercise restricted.
claims.assessment: Trial-specific randomized contrasts with uncertainty; no approved transfer to press or hybrid blocks.

support.result: 4SG minus CG +6.3 kg (95% CI 0.8 to 11.8); 6SG minus CG +14.5 kg (9.2 to 19.9); 6SG minus 4SG +8.2 kg (2.8 to 13.7).
support.restriction: Assigned whole-program contrasts over 12 weeks, not an isolated escalation effect or individualized policy.

claims.assertion: In the female trial, the two scheduled escalation groups improved leg-press 1RM more than the fixed-set group.
claims.limitations: 38 allocated, 30 completed; unequal starting and preparatory set counts; main-phase totals 264/252/336; no demonstrated equivalence in realized dose; manuscript requires version confirmation.
claims.assessment: Publisher abstract confirms direction; detailed effects extracted from manuscript. No feedback or hybrid transfer. Smaller progression arm accumulated fewer prescribed sets than CG; do not claim all escalation arms accumulated more.

support.locator: Manuscript Results, Muscular adaptations; Table 2 and Fig. 3
support.result: 2SG minus CG +15.7 kg (95% CI 1.1 to 30.3); 4SG minus CG +27.4 kg (12.5 to 42.3); 4SG minus 2SG +11.7 kg (-2.4 to 25.9).
support.restriction: Specific 12-week lower-body trajectories; not matched-dose causal isolation.

claims.assertion: The fitted meta-regression relates higher fractional weekly set volume to greater strength gains with strong diminishing returns.
claims.limitations: Aggregate mixed-experience model; varying endpoints and protocols; adjustment does not identify individual causal response; no timing/feedback comparison.
claims.assessment: 66 studies, 490 effects, 2020 participants for strength. Direct-only analyses qualitatively corroborate primary result per authors; verify OSF. Full-text reproduction version requires confirmation.

support.result: Marginal slope at mean fractional weekly volume 0.21% per set (95% CrI 0.16 to 0.26); reciprocal best fit.
support.restriction: Model-dependent mean association conditional on frequency, duration and training status, not a universal slope or dose limit.

claims.assertion: Trained men maintaining their prior weekly set count improved back-squat 1RM; the trial did not establish a difference in strength gains between maintenance and increases.
claims.limitations: 55 allocated, 29 completed; baseline strength imbalance; no significant group-by-time interaction; lack of significance is not equivalence; group main effect not a change contrast.
claims.assessment: Directly relevant habitual-dose comparator. Indexed paper excerpts only; direct between-group change intervals not extracted.

support.locator: Results and Discussion, maximal strength; baseline table
support.result: Pooled change about 22 kg; maintenance change about 32 kg; within-group effect sizes 0.86/0.73/0.72; no significant group-by-time interaction.
support.restriction: Do not claim superiority or equivalence; no threshold or hybrid transfer.

claims.assertion: Derived training strain was greater in the higher scheduled set progression conditions in the male Enes cohort.
claims.limitations: Derived metric contains exposure; same cohort as Enes strength trial; not a clinical fatigue, injury or overtraining endpoint; no decision intervention.
claims.assessment: Secondary same-cohort outcomes; do not count as independent evidence of strength adaptation.

support.result: 6S > 4S > FS, p < 0.001; effect magnitude/CI not extracted.
support.restriction: Derived strain only; not evidence of a fatigue-triggered adjustment benefit.

methods.question: strength-dose
methods.description: Retain a safe productive set dose as an admissible conservative option; consider a bounded volume change only after reviewing goals, achieved exposure, comparable performance, subjective burden, feasibility and competing priorities. Request information or defer when these are insufficient.
methods.provenance: Research Packet 002 RT-P02 revision 0.2, candidate methodology; not an empirical claim.
methods.tradeoffs: May forgo possible gains from additional sets or introduce unnecessary burden if escalated; no validated individual trigger, increment, window or ceiling. Requires parameter and human review.
